## 1. Headline findings (the three direct questions)

**Does `scripts/evaluate_autonomous_frontier.py` write files?**
Only with `--report <repo-relative-path>` (`write_report`, lines 1067–1070: `mkdir -p` + `write_text`). Without `--report` it writes **nothing** to the repo. All gate verification commands and known-bad replays execute inside a `tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(prefix="cre-frontier-evaluation-")` **copy** of the repo (`shutil.copytree` ignoring `.venv`/`__pycache__`/`.pytest_cache`, lines 998–1004); replayed commands get env `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, so no bytecode is written even in the copy. The real tree is only read: file/tree SHA-256 digests, `git rev-parse HEAD`, `git status --porcelain`. Stdout is restricted to exactly `PASS`, `FAIL`, or `BLOCKED_EXTERNAL` (fail-closed: any exception → `FAIL` with only the exception type name in the optional report).

**Is it deterministic / does re-running on a clean tree leave the tree clean?**
Yes, when run without `--report`. Determinism is enforced structurally: every verification command must exit 0 with exact stdout `PASS\n` and empty stderr, and `tree_digest` before/after each command inside the copy must be identical (`run_command`, lines 244–279) — so non-deterministic or tree-mutating verifiers fail by construction.
